title: Recover the failed boundary, not just the connection
description: Select an observed failure and a response. The trace shows whether identity, session state, authorization, and side-effect certainty are actually restored.

scenarios.label: Server returns HTTP 404 for the session
scenarios.detail: A Streamable HTTP request carries a previously valid MCP-Session-Id.
scenarios.safeConsequence: Discard the expired ID and send a fresh initialize request without a session ID.
scenarios.wrongConsequence: Reusing the old ID cannot revive server state and may create a retry loop.
evidence: The response is tied to a request carrying the old session ID
No tool request was accepted in a replacement session
The new initialize exchange negotiates version and capabilities again

scenarios.label: Connection drops after a write is sent
scenarios.detail: The server may have committed the side effect before its response reached the client.
scenarios.safeConsequence: Query by operation ID, then retry only if the dependency proves the write did not commit.
scenarios.wrongConsequence: A blind replay can duplicate a payment, message, ticket, or file mutation.
evidence: A stable operation or idempotency key identifies the intended effect
The dependency exposes committed, absent, or still-running state
The audit record links the original call and any safe replay

scenarios.label: Server rejects the token scope
scenarios.detail: The identity is known, but the current token cannot authorize the requested operation.
scenarios.safeConsequence: Explain the added scope, obtain user consent, and request a new audience-bound token.
scenarios.wrongConsequence: Retrying the same token or rebuilding only the MCP session leaves authorization unchanged.
evidence: The challenge names the required scope
The user sees the expanded permission before consent
The replacement token remains bound to the canonical MCP server resource

scenarios.label: A session ID arrives with a different user token
scenarios.detail: An attacker has obtained a valid-looking session ID but not the original user's authorization.
scenarios.safeConsequence: Reject the request, revoke or rotate the session, and investigate how the identifier leaked.
scenarios.wrongConsequence: Trusting the session ID as identity lets another subject impersonate the original client.
evidence: Authorization is verified independently on every inbound request
Server-side state binds the session to the authenticated subject
Session IDs are random, short-lived, protected, and revocable

scenarios.label: Progress continues but the request never finishes
scenarios.detail: The server emits progress often enough to reset an idle timer while consuming resources indefinitely.
scenarios.safeConsequence: Send cancellation, stop waiting, and enforce the maximum deadline even if progress continues.
scenarios.wrongConsequence: An endlessly renewed timeout allows a faulty server to hold client and server resources forever.
evidence: The request has an idle timeout and a separate absolute deadline
Cancellation and final status are recorded independently
A later retry follows the tool's completion and idempotency contract

actions.label: Start a fresh initialize exchange
actions.detail: Discard expired state and negotiate a new session without the old ID.

actions.label: Reconcile by operation ID
actions.detail: Check committed state before deciding whether a write may be replayed.

actions.label: Request visible scope step-up
actions.detail: Obtain new consent and a replacement token for the same MCP resource.

actions.label: Reject, revoke, and rotate
actions.detail: Treat the mismatch as a security event, not a recoverable client typo.

actions.label: Cancel at the absolute deadline
actions.detail: Stop waiting even when progress continues and contain resource use.

actions.label: Retry the same request immediately
actions.detail: Replay without changing authorization, session state, or completion evidence.
